newsitem.title: MEXICO: Gruma says corn-flour subsidies to change.
newsitem.headline: Gruma says corn-flour subsidies to change.

text.p: A top official at Gruma, parent company of Mexican corn flour producer Maseca, on Wednesday said an announcement of changes in the ceilings system of corn flour and other subsidies later in the day would be "positive for the industry."
"We're going to go ahead with the announcement this afternoon. We'll be announcing it at the same time as we are reporting first-quarter numbers," Chief Financial Officer Javier Velez told Reuters.
Earlier, Maseca canceled a planned news conference in which it was due to make the announcement. That sent Maseca's stock price, that had surged early in the day, into a trough.

Velez said it was only the news conference that was scrapped, not the announcement, correcting information from Maseca's press office, where an official said the announcement was postponed indefinitely.
"Today we'll be announcing changes in the ceilings system the government established and this announcement will be positive for the industry," he said.
He said the ceilings related to corn flour subsidies and some subsidies on tortillas.
